name: Browserbase
note: Headless browsers designed specifically for AI agents.
good: Handles captchas, proxies, and session management automatically. Great API.
bad: Expensive for high-volume scraping. Can sometimes be slower than raw Puppeteer.
price: Usage based. Starts around $20/mo for real usage.

name: Tavily
good: Returns clean text rather than just links. Reduces hallucination by grounding.
bad: Sometimes misses niche queries that Google would catch. Latency can spike.

name: Exa
good: Finds content by meaning rather than keywords. Great for finding blog posts and papers.
bad: Terrible for real-time news or 'what is the current stock price' queries.

name: Composio
good: One API key gives access to GitHub, Slack, Notion, etc.
bad: You are trusting a middleman with OAuth tokens. Documentation can be spotty.

name: E2B
note: Sandboxed cloud environments for AI to run code.
good: Secure code execution. Let your agent write and test Python safely.
bad: Startup time for the sandbox can add latency to the agent loop.
price: Usage based per second of compute.

name: Val Town
note: Social programming environment, great for quick AI webhooks.
good: Write a JS function, get an API endpoint instantly. Perfect for glue code.
bad: Not built specifically for AI, so you have to wire up the tool definitions yourself.
price: Free tier is great. Pro is $10/mo.

name: Apify
note: The heavy lifter for web scraping.
good: Pre-built actors for almost any site (Twitter, Instagram, Amazon).
bad: Actors often break when sites change UI. Pricing can be confusing (compute units).

name: Wolfram Alpha API
note: The OG tool for fixing LLM math capabilities.
good: Flawless computation and factual data retrieval.
bad: LLMs often struggle to format the queries perfectly for Wolfram's strict syntax.
price: Non-commercial free tier. Commercial requires contact.
